A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRS research, with matching authors, core formulation and experiments. Their complete main texts, appendices A–G, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original diffusion-model training and image-generation experiments in Section 5 and Appendix F, including FID, sFID, precision and recall.

after.justification: V4 retains original experiments and adds results including convergence analyses, scheduling sensitivity tests and evaluation of a cosine-based scheduling alternative.

M1.justification: The CRS equation, three discrepancy measures, adaptive training procedure and mixture construction are retained. V4 newly evaluates CRS-vx + vcos, but conventional-schedule mixing and the cosine conversion were already described in v3 Section 4.4. Pseudocode edits make existing feature extraction and optimization operations explicit.

E1.justification: The six datasets and overall image-generation coverage remain. However, CIFAR10 evaluation is reported as class-conditional in v3 Section 5 and Appendix F.3/Table 25, and as unconditional in v4 Section 5.1. The PDFs therefore report different task requirements for this retained dataset.

E2.justification: The pretrained EDM comparison is substantially revised: v4 Table 4 adds GITS and LD3, adds AYS for CIFAR10, and removes the EDM-schedule comparator rows present in v3 Tables 24–25. V4 Table 29 also adds an ImageNet comparison against LDM-4. GITS appearing elsewhere in v3 does not negate its addition to this comparison.

E3.justification: Within retained benchmarks, v4 removes pretrained-EDM evaluation at NFE = 50, expands sampler configurations and revises mixture exponents (v3 Table 7 versus v4 Table 12). Added analyses introduce EDM rho sweeps and tuned xi settings at NFE = 5. The stated endpoint alpha_e for computing vx changes from 10^-4 to 0.0 in v4 Table 9; this establishes a reported setting change, not that all experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V4 adds convergence comparisons on Horse and Church (Figures 12–13), EDM rho sensitivity tests (Table 20), low-NFE xi tuning (Tables 27–28), and evaluation of the cheaper cosine alternative (Table 7). These substantially expand the questions investigated. Existing mixture sensitivity analyses remain, while v3's standalone CRS-vFID exponent plot, Figure 4, is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new convergence plots do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and most appendix benchmark values remain unchanged, but pretrained-EDM results are replaced and substantial new entries appear. FFHQ DPM-Solver++ CRS FIDs at NFE = 10/20 change from 4.70/2.87 to 5.35/3.10 with revised hyperparameters, so this is not an established same-setting deterioration. New results include FID 6.96 with xi = 2.2 on latent Bedroom at NFE = 5 and ImageNet FID 9.67 at NFE = 250 (v4 Tables 27 and 29).

T1.justification: V4 corrects the joint-distribution definition by integrating out x0 (Appendix B, Equation 38 versus v3 Equation 37). It also removes the minus sign from the main CRS expansion (v4 Equation 8 versus v3 Equation 7), although the negative-slope scheduling ODE remains. These are limited mathematical revisions; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution—general scheduling for training and sampling—and the LSUN Horse FID 2.03 claim remain. V4's abstract and introduction explicitly delimit the contribution as an empirically validated framework without a complete theoretical justification connecting distributional change to sample quality. The conclusion also emphasizes recommended default configurations.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: it connects low-NFE sensitivity to the continuous-time approximation, acknowledges LD3's stronger sampling performance and CRS's tuning cost, and discusses missing theoretical guarantees, CFG evaluation, prediction parameterizations and transformer architectures. These go beyond v3's brief limitations paragraph, although some new superiority statements exceed the table evidence.

D1.justification: V4 adds LDM repository access information, identifies the GITS evaluation implementation and EDM feature-extractor source, and clarifies pseudocode. It also omits v3 Appendix E.3's explicit CRS sampling boundary settings. Most newly formatted hyperparameter information and hardware/training-time values were already disclosed in v3.

R1.justification: V4 broadens the related-work taxonomy from three acceleration strategies to five, connects CRS to flow matching and rectified flow, and explicitly positions AYS-related approaches as special cases. Added literature includes LD3, score-optimal schedules, improved training schedules, Diffusion Transformers and LPIPS. This materially expands research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: The title and most main-text and appendix prose are rewritten. 'Distance metrics' becomes 'discrepancy measures'; contributions, background and implementation explanations are expanded, with new subsection organization and a substantially restructured limitations discussion. These changes extend well beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V4 changes the document template and extensively reorganizes displays. It consolidates pretrained-EDM comparisons into Table 4, splits large Church and ImageNet tables by sampler type, adds analysis and hyperparameter tables, and replaces two earlier plots with convergence figures. Existing benchmark displays are redistributed, while all seven generated-image grids remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 improves practical assessment through convergence analyses, stronger comparison methods, tuning checks and validation of the cheaper cosine alternative, alongside clearer theoretical and applicability limits. These gains are tempered by new overstatements: Table 20 shows EDM beating CRS at NFE = 10 with DPM-Solver++ (4.73 versus 4.88), despite claiming otherwise. The net improvement is useful but limited.
